title: Transformations of Graphs
seo_title: Year 11 Maths: Transformations of Graphs Worksheets (GCSE)
standard_text: Sketch translations and reflections of a given function: y = f(x) + a, y = f(x + a), y = −f(x) and y = f(−x).
meta_desc: Free Year 11 GCSE maths worksheets on translations, reflections and stretches of graphs y = f(x). 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Inside the bracket the graph moves the opposite way.
key_sub: y = f(x − a) + b is a translation by the vector (a, b).
body_html:
How it works

For a graph y = f(x):

  • y = f(x) + a is a translation by the vector (0, a): up a.
  • y = f(x + a) is a translation by (−a, 0): left a. Inside the bracket the change is the opposite way.
  • y = −f(x) is a reflection in the x-axis; y = f(−x) is a reflection in the y-axis.
Example

Describe y = f(x − 3) + 2.

Inside: right 3

Outside: up 2

Answer: translation by the vector (3, 2)

Example

(2, 5) is on y = f(x). Where is it on y = f(x + 3) − 1?

Left 3, down 1

Answer: (−1, 4)

Common mistakes

  • Moving right for f(x + 3). It moves left 3.
  • Putting the vertical change inside the bracket.
  • Mixing up −f(x) (reflection in the x-axis) and f(−x) (reflection in the y-axis).

faq.q: How do you translate a graph to the right?
faq.a: Replace x with (x − a). For example, y = f(x − 4) is y = f(x) moved 4 units right.
It reflects the graph in the x-axis. A minus inside, y = f(−x), reflects it in the y-axis.

faq.q: How do you write a translation as a vector?
faq.a: The top number is the move right (negative for left) and the bottom number is the move up (negative for down). y = f(x − 2) + 5 is the vector (2, 5).
